messages:
nina: Quick report — customer hit what looks like duplicate token lines when their client reconnected during a streaming request that triggered a tool_call. They saw a provisional row left behind plus a confirmed row after reconnect.

meera: Can you drop the trace id & minimal repro?

nina: trace=trace-qqq-9. Simplified flow: start streaming -> server emits partial chunks -> tool_call invoked (pause stream) -> client reconnects (transport-level reconnect) while router chooses fallback model -> stream resumes. Ledger shows provisional (model=redwood-ultra, session=abc, tokens=120) and confirmed (model=redwood-small-quant, session=abc, tokens=95).

jonathan: So same session id but different model -> we are keying provisioning by (session, model, window) which causes both rows to exist.

leo: Did the client reuse the same session token on reconnect? if not we get multiple sessions and double billing is obvious.

nina: They reused session token. The router changed route context (model_tag and route_version).

alex: Important nuance: provisional rows have a short TTL and usually get swept or stitched. But our stitcher assumes contiguous model_tag. When model_tag switches mid-window we create a new stitch target and never migrate provisional from the older model to the new one.

meera: Two classes of fixes: 1) Prevent model swap if a tool_call or client reconnect is in progress (routing affinity), 2) Make ledger stitching model-agnostic for provisional rows (stitch by session + segment id), 3) UI: surface a consolidated charge and an explanation so customers aren't confused.

jonathan: For (2) we could add a new, optional attribution key field session_segment_id generated at stream start and preserved across reconnects and tool_call boundaries. Ledger would accept provisional rows tagged with either (model-specific key) or the session_segment_id and stitch by segment id when present. Migration job can then collapse double-entries safely.

leo: Generating session_segment_id requires changes in router -> client side headers and all proxies. Might be invasive but elegant.

alex: Short-term we should avoid schema churn. Proposal: Add a temporary reconciler that looks for rows with same session & overlapping time windows and a provisional->confirmed pattern, then coalesce them into a single confirmed row and write an audit entry. This is best-effort and idempotent if we mark migrated provisional rows with a migration_tag.

meera: I like two-phase: canary router affinity (deny model swap during active tool_call or within reconnect grace window) + reconciler to clean up historical data. Then medium-term add session_segment_id and change attribution key.

jonathan: Reconciler design notes: scan last 72h for (session) where provisional exists and a confirmed entry with overlapping window and total tokens less than sum(provisional+confirmed) -> create combined confirmed = max(tokens) or prefer confirmed tokens? we should prefer confirmed tokens but ensure customer-facing total equals the largest contiguous coverage. Also attach metadata: merged_from = [row_ids], migration_id, reconcile_ts. Mark provisionals as migrated.

leo: Edgecases: partial refunds, invoices that already exported, and customers reviewing raw ledger. Console should show both rows but visually collapse them with a single line item and a tooltip: "Merged by reconciliation due to mid-request routing fallback."

alex: Billing export impact: we should not rewrite finalized invoices. Reconciler should only operate on non-invoiced windows. For invoiced charges we must create a credit line instead of rewriting.

meera: Ops note: will add a router feature flag preventing model swap when tool_call in progress or within X seconds of transport reconnect. Default: off. Canary on internal org.

jonathan: I'll prototype reconciler job and the migration markers. Need to guarantee idempotency & visibility. I'll also update ledger row schema to accept an optional migrated_by field (string) — note: flat JSON row, but we can add top-level column.

nina: UX ask: please surface reconciler run history in console billing page and an explanation for any collapsed rows. Product will write copy.

billing-bot: scheduled job -> reconciler-scan/6071114000 (auto)

alex: Action items: meera -> router flag + canary; jonathan -> reconciler prototype + migration schema; leo -> audit all places that inject model_tag into attribution key; nina -> collect customer repro and verify post-reconcile; alex -> coordinate product copy & invoice guard.

meera: I'll push a small router patch today and flip flag for the internal canary.

jonathan: Starting prototype now. Will post design doc soon.

leo: Will run grep for attribution key usage and open a PR list.

nina: Thanks team, will report back once customer confirms fix or we have reconciler results.
